correctness.rationale: For T=U|T|, decompose H=ker(T)⊕H0, let A=|T||H0 injective and M=||A||. Spectral projection E_A({0})=0 although 0 can be continuous spectrum. Partition σ(A)\{0} into finitely many Borel sets of diameter<eps, assign positive representatives and M on the top cell; the bounded Borel step B=0⊕sum_j a_j E_A(Delta_j) is positive finite spectrum, in W*(|T|), injective on H0 and norm M, ||B−|T|||<eps. With S=UB, S*S=B² since U*U=support(B), and S has same true polar factor U, same kernel and exact norm. Selfadjoint finite-spectrum B attains norm on every reducing subspace, hence B in β(H), S in β0(H). Independent 4×4 spectral toy example confirms simultaneous zero kernel, top norm and ||step−A||=1/1000; not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Fixed-polar-factor norm-density is a natural structural refinement in operator theory: it approximates the modulus inside its own von Neumann algebra while preserving kernel multiplicity and exact norm, constraints useful when norm approximation must not change the polar orientation or null space. The new assertion is an all-operators density lemma and not a fabricated compact/finite-rank perturbation or arbitrary sliced calculation. Although it uses standard Borel functional calculus, preserving the three exact properties simultaneously gives an independently useful and motivated stronger approximation theorem; no paper-sized extension or formal proof is required.
